prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / precise-object-edit.
Edit the supplied concept image. The user likes the restrained exhibition-like UI, but asks for a DIFFERENT actual pottery WORKSHOP environment and much clearer readability on the right. Produce one polished 16:9 concept screenshot.

Preserve: the unbranded embedded-module format with NO top bar, NO logo, NO branding; elegant Chinese serif heading, thin outlined low-radius controls; left vessel/right tools layout; the jar's rounded shape and realistic matte unglazed bisque material; the same content and unobtrusive process/control strip. Do not turn this into a big frosted-glass dashboard or chunky physical buttons.

Replace the whole environment with a clearly recognizable contemporary artisan CERAMICS WORKSHOP, distinct from the cozy exhibition window scene in the supplied image. Remove the wooden lattice window, garden/leaf shadows, decorative branch vase, tea-like cup and linen-table vignette. This is a working studio: a broad finely detailed pale worn-wood workbench occupying the left two thirds, the bisque jar on a simple circular potter's work bat, a few real glaze brushes laid flat, a small sponge and two unobtrusive glaze mixing jars at the far left. Behind the left half, softly blurred open shelves of unfinished bowls and small raw vessels, a modest pottery wheel further back, a quiet off-white lime-plaster wall. Daylight arrives diffusely from a high studio window outside the crop, balanced natural light, subtle warm shadows. Fine wood grain and tactile chalky ceramics, clean and cared for rather than cluttered or industrially dirty. No antique Chinese window, no gallery plinth, no surreal colored fabric backdrop, no giant props.

COMPOSITION and readability: main jar remains center-left, about 45% image height, matte warm ivory, fine pores and delicate throwing rings. No glossy glaze or decorative crackle.
The rightmost 28% must be a clean, softly lit, nearly uniform pale warm-gray PLASTER WALL area, with absolutely no props, leaf shadows, window silhouettes, high-contrast texture, shelf lines or table edge behind the text and controls. Have the workbench end before the right tool column or recede away from it. This visually quiet wall is part of the workshop, not an enclosing UI panel. Keep plenty of breathing space between the vessel and right column.
Right-column text must be highly legible: solid dark charcoal-brown, not semi-transparent, no light beige lettering on beige. Slightly increase small label font sizes and use clear spacing. Thin borders/sliders should be visible medium warm-gray, not ghosted hairlines. Increase the main button contrast with a clearly visible dark outlined border, solid dark text and a subtle neutral translucent fill; all controls share the same lightweight flat translucent material. No large enclosing card. No bevels, no raised clay knobs, no heavy shadows, no greens in the interface.

Render exactly this readable simplified Chinese:
small kicker: "02 / 施釉"
serif heading: "为素坯施釉"
subline: "颜色藏在窑火之后"
status: "素烧瓷坯 · 尚未施釉"
tabs: "釉色" "笔触", one fine active underline
palette caption: "烧后釉色参考"
three small flat reference swatches with dark labels: "天青" "月白" "铜红"; ensure the near-white swatch has a thin visible border.
slider labels: "笔刷大小" and "施釉厚度"; dark visible tracks and small simple circular handles.
primary outlined button: "进入烧制 →"
secondary action: "返回选坯"
bottom-left compact process strip: "01 选坯" "02 施釉" "03 烧制" "04 出窑"; one short active underline, readable text on quiet background.
bottom-right compact outlined strip: "旋转" "缩放" "复位"; readable dark text on the light background.

Maintain the understated typographic language of the original concept and three exhibition screens; change scene identity and improve legibility, not the entire interface direction. A full-screen UI mockup, no browser chrome, no comparison layout, no labels describing the design, no watermark.
